Local chess trainer: play Stockfish with real clock presets, drill your openings against a bot that follows the book and flags where you left theory, and review your games from PGN, Chess.com or Lichess with an evaluation bar. Chess960 included. In 27 languages, all in one Docker image. It runs on your own machine (amd64 or arm64), with no accounts and no internet needed to play.

## Run

You need Docker with Compose.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nielsencampos/chess-trainer.git
cd chess-trainer
docker compose up --build
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>.

Or, without cloning, run the published image (amd64 or arm64); your games stay in `./data`:

```bash
mkdir -p data
docker run -d --init --name chess-trainer -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
  -v "$PWD/data:/app/data" ghcr.io/nielsencampos/chess-trainer:latest
```

The app is published on loopback only, because it has no login. To reach it from another device, set `CHESS_TRAINER_BIND=0.0.0.0`, on a network you trust, and list the names you will open it by in `CHESS_TRAINER_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (such as `192.168.0.10,chess.lan`): the app answers only to `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` otherwise. `CHESS_TRAINER_PORT` changes the port.

**Desktop app (preview):** the same app in its own window, without Docker, for Windows, macOS and Linux. To download and install it, see [HOW_TO_INSTALL.fr.md](HOW_TO_INSTALL.fr.md); how it is built is in [desktop/](desktop/README.md). Docker stays the reference way to run it.

## How it works

The full guide, with pictures, is in [docs/HELP.fr.md](docs/HELP.fr.md), the same as the Help screen in the app, and who made it and why is in [docs/ABOUT.fr.md](docs/ABOUT.fr.md). A summary:

1. Pick your color and the lines to drill, from all 3,865 lines of the book. Search by name, ECO or moves. Each selected line has the same chance of being drawn.
2. The bot plays the drawn line. If you play a move from another selected line, it follows you.
3. A move outside the selected lines is a deviation: it is recorded with the expected moves and shown at the end of the game.
4. When the line ends or someone leaves theory, Stockfish takes over at the selected level.

Unchecking "Show moves" hides the move list and the opening name, headings included, during a game, so you can write on paper. They come back at the end.

Beyond openings:

- **Clocks:** bullet, and the blitz, rapid and classical presets of a DGT 3000 clock, or no clock.
- **Chess960:** roll one of the 960 starting positions, or paste its FEN, and play Stockfish.
- **Saved games:** every game is saved. Filter them, export them as PGN, review them move by move, or start a new game from any of their moves (not yet from a Chess960 game).
- **Import:** paste PGN, upload a file, or fetch a player's public games from Chess.com or Lichess. The review shows the PGN's evaluations, classifications, clocks, comments and side lines.
- **Evaluation bar:** Stockfish's evaluation while reviewing, and at the end of a game. It is a quick check, not a full analysis: for that, export the PGN to Chess.com or Lichess.
- **Scoresheet:** a printable A4 scoresheet, modeled on an official one, to write your moves by hand during long games. It is not an official scoresheet: it is for training only.
- **Help:** how to use every screen, in the app's menu.

Chess Trainer is for training. Never use it, or any engine, during a game against another person.

**Current state:** the book and games are in DuckDB (`data/chess-trainer.duckdb`). Bot levels are provisional. The UI is in 27 languages. See the [project brief](docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md) for what comes next.

## The book

The bot's book is in `openings/`, one JSON file per opening family, loaded into DuckDB on start (a few seconds the first time). It starts with all 3,865 lines of the [Lichess openings catalog](https://github.com/lichess-org/chess-openings). Any line plays with either color. The catalog lists named positions, not recommended replies, so lines are often short and the engine plays on from there. They can be extended by pull request, recording the source. The format is in [the brief, §6](docs/PROJECT_BRIEF.md).

The database lives in `./data`, which the container writes as UID 1000. To back it up, stop the app and copy the file. Every move is saved there, so an unfinished game continues when you open the page again, even after a restart. Clocks stop while the app is closed.

## Update Stockfish

The image uses the latest official Stockfish release at build time. To update:

```bash
docker compose build --pull
docker compose up -d
```

To pin a version (`sf_19` or newer; older releases have no universal or Linux arm64 binary):

```bash
STOCKFISH_VERSION=sf_19 docker compose build
```

The running version is in the page footer and at `/api/health`. If the build reports a GitHub rate limit, wait an hour: the limit is 60 API requests per hour without a token.

## Develop

Needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Test commands and conventions are in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md), and how to contribute in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

```bash
uv sync
uv run pytest
```

The pictures in Help are screenshots of the app in each language. After a visible UI change, make them again against a running app (it plays and resigns games):

```bash
uv run python scripts/help_media.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

`docs/HELP*.md` and `docs/ABOUT*.md` are written from the Help and About screens' strings, and `README*.md` and `HOW_TO_INSTALL*.md` from `i18n/docs/`. After changing them, run `uv run python scripts/help_docs.py` and `uv run python scripts/readme_docs.py`; a test fails while the files are out of date.
